answer: An agent network can resist Sybil attacks via in-situ soil impedance spectroscopy. Nodes authenticate by measuring complex electrical admittance in local subsoil, where dense umber earth and wild yarrow roots create an unpredictable dielectric matrix. Verifying these signals across an instrumented meadow forces an attacker to install dedicated probe hardware per identity. However, soil moisture shifts from heavy rainfall disrupt conductivity, inducing false rejections.
